SCAST is a research frontier pending complex-codebase scanner and rendering-data evaluation.

Plugin ecosystem mapped; extension contract boundary remains unresolved.

Persist verified Topo proof-of-concept frontier.

PMD is a multi-language diagnostics and duplicate-code enrichment candidate, not the topology extractor.

Operator rejected proceeding to proof of concept. Required a structured capability report of all scanning tools first, to inform which tool a component-map prototype is built around. Fixture repo to be nominated by operator later.
Frontier changed from needs-proof-of-concept to needs-research by operator correction. Capability matrix precedes prototype.

Dispatched six bounded research threads with one shared capability schema: language-neutral substrates, TypeScript extractors, TypeScript generators, whole-product precedents, layout and render engines, per-language adapter coverage.
Cycle 4 evidence pass found no new evidence. Topo repository still has zero commits and only an untracked skill log. GitHub still lists one issue, unchanged since before discovery began.

Operator added Sokrates as a seventh research thread. Dispatched with the whole-product precedent schema, focused on logical decomposition, multi-language breadth technique, static report output, and JSON consumability.

Operator added CodeGraph as an eighth research thread. Dispatched with a graph-model schema focus: node and edge types, stable identity mechanism, storage and external dependencies, incremental reindex, plus an explicit credibility check on README claims versus source evidence.

Arkit is precedent-only: glob-pattern component config is adoptable but its model is never serialized and it requires Java. Codebase-map is a partial core scanner with real incremental update and typed ProjectIndex JSON. Neither provides stable IDs or line-column anchoring; codebase-map rewrites timestamps every scan.

Operator added aloc as a ninth research thread. Dispatched with an existence-verification gate and a structure-versus-metrics classification question, comparing it against cloc, scc, and tokei as a possible cheap first-pass sizing scanner.

Tree-sitter is a viable core scanner substrate. Kythe rates enrichment-adapter only: it has VName stable identities but requires Bazel, publishes no npm package, is batch-only, and its TypeScript indexer has no commit in about seventeen months.

Dependency-cruiser is the only one of the three producing component-level structure today, via collapsePattern, --collapse, and the archi reporter, and it ships a documented CI-tested JSON schema. Ts-morph alone gives line and column anchoring. Madge offers a flat undocumented file graph.

Elkjs plus a renderer gives deterministic build-time layered layout with first-class compound nesting. No library solves stable incremental layout: elkjs tracks it as an open issue and fCoSE fixedNodeConstraint is the closest documented mechanism. Topo must build position preservation at the application layer.

Operator nominated the static-analysis catalog for a dedicated crawl. Dispatched to assess it as machine-readable adapter-discovery data and to sweep for structural tools not already researched. Scc was folded into the existing aloc thread as a first-class subject.

Operator added a licensing constraint: Topo ships as personal open source on a personal GitHub account, so every dependency must be license-compatible. Dispatched a dedicated licensing thread analyzing linked-library, subprocess, browser-shipped, and data-reuse modes. Elkjs EPL-2.0 and PlantUML GPL flagged as priority risks.

No existing product combines static output, derived-from-source model, coordinated views, and agent queryability. CodeAtlas Live needs a permanent daemon. Structurizr is an authored-model tool and architecturally incompatible with a scan-generate pipeline. Topo occupies a real gap.

CodeGraph is precedent-only: four commits in one day, AI-authored, unused declared dependencies, and README claims exceeding source. Its enumerated fifty node labels and thirty-six relationship types, and its entity identifier scheme of kind plus normalized path plus qualified name, are directly reusable. Neo4j is a hard dependency that conflicts with static output.

Sokrates already achieves roughly eighty-five percent of the intended static offline report output from a derived model, and supports multiple coexisting logical decompositions defined by folder depth, filter rules, or content-derived meta rules. Its breadth is regex heuristic by design, with no TypeScript dependency analysis, and its JSON sits inside a zip with no published schema.

Adapter coverage is uneven. Go and Rust are strongest because go list and cargo metadata are built in with documented JSON. Python and Java are strong. C sharp, C and C plus plus, and PHP are workable but need a custom harness. Ruby is genuinely weak. PMD is a quality overlay only: it has no cross-file dependency resolution and cannot build a component map.

Catalog is roughly ninety-four percent linters and security scanners, with about fifteen of five hundred ninety-two entries useful for structure extraction, and its taxonomy lacks any output-format or emits-graph field, so automated consumption is not worth the cost. Best missed find is Depends, an MIT reusable multi-language dependency extraction framework. ENRE-ts is a purpose-built TypeScript entity-relation extractor but is LGPL-2.1 and Node 16 to 18 only.

Scc wins the fast first-pass counting role: MIT, three hundred sixty-six languages, richest per-file JSON including a complexity estimate, best distribution, and version four released the day before research. Its languages.json is directly reusable as a language-detection asset under MIT. Aloc is dormant with eighteen stars, but its core, test, infra, and docs role classification is a novel idea Topo can implement natively.

Operator reopened the host implementation language. TypeScript on Node was decided in cycle three and is no longer locked; Python or another runtime is acceptable. Dispatched a host-runtime research thread comparing Node, Python, Go, and Rust on tree-sitter bindings, TypeScript semantic access, layout options, distribution friction, determinism hazards, and plugin ecosystem.

Operator clarified that TypeScript remains preferred and wins ties, and that the real question is opportunity cost. Host-runtime thread reframed to identify only capabilities genuinely forfeited by staying on TypeScript, gated on a three-part test requiring material value, no viable subprocess path, and no adequate TypeScript equivalent. Stack-graphs and SCIP flagged as priority leads.

Most candidates are permissive. Elkjs is dual EPL-2.0 or GPL-3.0-or-later, usable via the EPL arm with attribution shipped in generated output. Cloc is GPL-2.0 and jQAssistant and Neo4j Community are GPL-3.0, so all are subprocess only. ENRE-ts is LGPL-2.1 and must never be bundled. MIT remains the recommended license for Topo.

CodeGraph and the Structurizr DSL repository have no license file despite a badge claim, which makes them all rights reserved and unusable as dependencies. CodeGraph was already precedent-only, so the practical impact is limited to forbidding any code reuse from it.

Licensing thread reported codebase-map as repository not found and license unverifiable, contradicting the generators thread which read its source directly. Verified against primary source: the GitHub API returned 403 rate limited, not 404, while the repository page and raw package.json both return 200 and declare MIT. Codebase-map exists and is MIT.

TypeScript confirmed as host. The forfeit list holds one item, stack-graphs, and GitHub has abandoned it with no WASM or Node binding ever published. SCIP is a real but partial path: scip-typescript runs on our own runtime and TypeScript bindings exist, but SCIP is symbol level only and carries no component topology.

Compiled the full capability matrix covering thirty-four tools across twelve research threads, with role, runtime, license, consumption mode, output, component capability, anchoring, incrementality, and verdict, plus per-language coverage, license classes, confirmed gaps, and evidence index.

A rename is a refactor and triggers a topo rebuild. No rename detection, no move heuristics, and no content-similarity matching will be built. This removes the hardest half of the stable identity problem and also answers when a saved view is invalidated rather than rebalanced.

Identity and version fingerprint are separated. Identity is path plus qualified symbol name and must resist change. Fingerprint reacts to every change and drives skip-unchanged scanning and changed badges. Conflating them would destroy saved layout positions on every edit.

Topo snapshots are anchored to a commit. Git already provides the fingerprint: a blob SHA is a per-file content hash and a tree SHA covers a whole directory, so unchanged subtrees can be skipped without hashing anything ourselves. The commit anchor also supplies topology diffing and a spine for the delivery activity view.

Dirty working tree handling is undecided. Options are requiring a clean tree, generating against HEAD and ignoring uncommitted edits, or generating against the working tree and marking the snapshot as HEAD plus dirty. The third is the current lean but is not decided.

Saved layouts are not priority zero. Deterministic layout ships first and drag-to-persist is deferred. This removes stable incremental layout, saved-view merge policy, and invalidate-versus-rebalance rules from scope.
Path-based identity confirmed. Semantic and content-derived component boundaries are explicitly out of version one scope, which is a deliberate trade rather than an oversight.

Lean into chosen SDKs deeply, but only inside the adapter. The canonical graph stays ours and no dependency vocabulary crosses that boundary. This makes the canonical schema the load-bearing decision of the project.

Sokrates is precedent-only for version one because it has no TypeScript dependency analysis, ships JSON inside a zip without a schema, and requires a JVM. Revisit later as a breadth or delivery-activity adapter.

Operator nominated the mermaid repository as the proof-of-concept target. It is a pnpm monorepo with nine packages and roughly eight hundred thirteen TypeScript files, giving path-aligned components at real scale, and it ships a layout package that uses elkjs.
Cycle four handoff persisted and reread successfully. Alignment status is corrected then verified. Frontier is needs-proof-of-concept with the mermaid repository as the named target.

Routing to proof-of-concept with a bounded question: can a local TypeScript scan of the mermaid monorepo produce a deterministic component schematic, survive a content edit with identities intact, and publish a static page.

Prototype scanned the mermaid monorepo, built a canonical graph, laid it out with elkjs headless, and published a self-contained static page. Seven hundred thirty modules across nine packages scanned in about three point six seconds; end to end about four point nine seconds.

Determinism confirmed. Two consecutive generations produced byte-identical graph, layout, and HTML for both decompositions, including elkjs coordinates. Identity survival confirmed: after a content edit all node identities matched and zero nodes moved.

Three real defects found. Dependency-cruiser under-scans a bare directory argument and requires an explicit glob. A single root tsconfig silently drops monorepo packages. Git tree SHAs only fingerprint committed state, so a dirty tree needs git hash-object on working files instead.

Package-level decomposition produced eight components and zero edges because cross-package imports cannot resolve without node_modules. The second decomposition inside the mermaid source produced a genuinely informative map including a circular dependency between diagrams and diagram-api, which validates supporting multiple competing decompositions.

Throwaway workspace deleted. Prototype source, canonical graphs, layouts, and two rendered pages preserved as evidence in the session workspace. Target repository verified clean with zero modified files.

Cross-package edges are derivable from package manifests without node_modules. Six workspace dependency edges were extracted directly from package.json files, so manifest declarations can supply package-level topology that module resolution cannot.

Decomposition dominance is measurable. The mermaid package holds five hundred thirty-two of six hundred sixty-three scanned files, about eighty percent, which suggests a ratio threshold could automatically trigger a drill-down decomposition rather than requiring hand configuration.

Cycle five frontier. The stack is proven and adopted. Two design questions remain: how to combine manifest-derived and resolution-derived edges into one canonical model, and what rule selects decompositions automatically. Both are design questions rather than tooling questions.
Cycle five handoff persisted and reread. Proof of concept adopted; two design questions carried forward into cycle six.

Canonical edges carry provenance. Manifest-declared and resolution-derived edges are both preserved rather than merged, with a declared-as qualifier distinguishing runtime, peer, and dev. Their disagreement becomes a product feature surfacing unused and phantom dependencies, and neither source vocabulary leaks into the model.

Decomposition selection is dominance triggered rather than configured. When one component exceeds a file-share threshold, an additional decomposition drills into it and recurses to a depth cap. Applied to mermaid this reproduces exactly the two decompositions built by hand during the prototype, improving on Sokrates which requires hand-authored decompositions.

Agent overstated an undeclared dependency finding. The mermaid package is declared by layout-elk as a peer and dev dependency, which is the standard plugin pattern, so that case is consistent rather than a defect. The provenance mechanism still holds and this instance validates it.
The dominance threshold of roughly forty percent is invented rather than measured. Calibrating it needs several repositories with different shapes, not the single monorepo tested so far.
Cycle six handoff persisted and reread. Edge provenance and dominance-triggered decomposition are verified decisions.

Frontier is ready. The canonical graph schema is settled enough to hand to specification. One question stays open in parallel: calibrating the dominance threshold across repositories of differing shape.
Cycle seven opened. Frontier was ready, but the operator re-entered discovery, so the cycle targets the weakest claim in the cycle six handoff: the uncalibrated forty percent dominance threshold.
Measured component file share at depth one and two across six local repositories of differing shape: mermaid, d3, wezterm, herdr, gstack, agent-skills.

Top component share is bimodal. Dominant repositories measure seventy nine to eighty nine percent and non dominant ones measure twelve to twenty five percent. No repository lands between twenty six and forty eight percent, so any threshold from forty to sixty separates them identically. Threshold precision is not the risk.

Dominance triggered decomposition is one sided and fails on wezterm, which has fifty two flat crates with a top share of twelve point seven percent. The rule never fires and the engineer receives a fifty two node hairball. The real missing rule is a cardinality trigger that aggregates rather than decomposes.

Dominance is blind to component kind. On gstack the dominant component is test at forty eight point eight percent, so the rule fires and drills into tests rather than production code. A pseudo component for files sitting directly under a parent can also dominate.
Small repositories need a floor. The d3 checkout has fifteen scannable files and any decomposition of it is noise.

Operator reframed decomposition from a selection problem into a navigation problem. Topo presents one expandable tree that the human drills into and zooms out of, so the product never has to choose a single correct decomposition. Dominance triggered decomposition is retired as a trigger.
External packages are terminal nodes. A dependency on an external package is shown but never expanded, because decomposing it belongs to that package own topo graph in its own repository.

Measured per node fan out across six repositories to test whether interactive drill down is legible without any decomposition rule. Median fan out is one to four everywhere and only three to twenty percent of nodes exceed fifteen children.

Drill down is legible by default, which validates the navigation reframe and removes the need for a global decomposition threshold. Wide nodes are the exception rather than the rule, so a legibility rule is only needed as local relief on individual wide nodes.

The operator described drilling from application to layers to interfaces to implementation, but layers are frequently not path aligned. A directory derived tree will show directories at the level where the operator expects layers, which conflicts with the locked path aligned components constraint.

The wezterm root has fifty two children and no parent structure above them, so a wide root remains unsolved under the navigation model. The gstack test directory has three hundred seventy one children.

The repository is always the root of the component browser tree. Every repository therefore has at least one keyable root, wide roots are structurally impossible, and multiple frameworks or patterns inside one repository can be pulled apart beneath a single common root.

Layers in the component browser are logical and inferred from code rather than derived from folders. Folder derived layers remain valid for other views but not for this one, so the component browser tree is path free at every level and the earlier path aligned components constraint no longer governs it.

A manifest probe of wezterm reported zero intra workspace edges because crates declare dependencies through cargo workspace inheritance rather than inline path tables. Correct parsing found two hundred sixty three edges. This is the third instance of a scanner silently returning zero or partial results while reporting success, after the dependency cruiser bare directory case and the root tsconfig case.

Deterministic layer inference is achievable without clustering. Strongly connected component condensation followed by longest path level assignment is fully deterministic under sorted iteration, so no randomized community detection is required and the determinism guarantee survives.

Applied to wezterm the inference produced fifteen levels across sixty eight acyclic crates, reducing root fan out from fifty two to fifteen. Two levels remain wide at twenty one and sixteen crates, so inferred layering improves legibility at the root but does not by itself keep every level legible.

Topological depth is not the same as a semantic layer. Fifteen levels is far more than the three to five layers an architect normally names, and the level holding twenty one leaf utility crates is a depth bucket rather than a coherent layer.

Depth is the truth and naming is cosmetic. Topo infers the logical view from how modules relate rather than from folders, because a file browser already shows folders. Configuration is deliberately minimal and confined to the root dot topo directory plus the occasional development dependency in the project.
Measured level stability under single edge perturbation on the wezterm crate graph across two hundred sixty three removal trials and four hundred addition trials.

Determinism does not imply stability. Removing one edge leaves every level unchanged in eighty three percent of trials, but two percent of edges form a spine whose removal relevels thirty four to forty four of sixty eight crates. Adding an edge is roughly six times more disruptive with a mean of seven crates moved and nineteen percent of trials moving more than ten.

The instability is confined to derived strata rather than identity. Nodes keep their stable identity, so agent references and saved references survive a relevelling and only the layer assignment churns.

The sensitivity analysis is itself a candidate product feature. A small set of spine edges determines the shape of the entire logical view, which is high leverage architectural information an engineer cannot otherwise see.

Stability was measured only on wezterm, which is acyclic at crate level. A heavily cyclic codebase condenses into fewer and fatter levels, so the logical view may degrade exactly where the code is least healthy and most in need of a map. This remains untested.

Alignment offered and verified. The operator parked cyclic codebases as a later discovery item, chose to assume hierarchical codebases for now, and directed discovery to continue until the work is clear enough to implement autonomously. The agent flagged that the mermaid prototype target already contains a cycle rather than letting the assumption stand unchallenged.
Cycle seven handoff persisted and reread. Navigation, repository as root, inferred logical layers, and deterministic level assignment are verified decisions.
Cycle seven measurement scripts copied from the temporary directory into the session workspace so the handoff references remain resolvable after a reboot.

Frontier is needs more evidence rather than ready. The operator declined to move to specification and asked for continued discovery until the work is clear enough to ship autonomously. The largest unexamined area is the symbol level below modules, where interfaces and implementations live and where nothing has been exercised.

Cycle eight opened on the symbol level below modules, testing read only whether the interface and implementation levels the operator described actually exist in real typescript before recommending a prototype there.
Measured export shape and interface implementation rate across five repositories covering four thousand exports.

The interface to implementation drill path does not exist in real typescript. Interfaces are twenty percent of exports in mermaid and gstack but only one point six percent and zero point seven percent of them have any implementing class. They are data shapes such as configuration and props rather than architectural seams. Two repositories declare no interfaces at all and functions dominate everywhere.

The operator almost certainly meant interface in the informal sense of a public exported surface rather than the typescript interface keyword. Under that reading the level below a module is its exported surface of functions, types, classes, and constants, and the level below that is its internal symbols and the call graph among them. Implements relationships are a java and c sharp shape and are close to absent here.

The export measurement understates functions because arrow functions assigned to exported constants are counted as constants. Exported constants reach forty four percent in mermaid, so the split between data constants and arrow function exports is unresolved.

The operator confirmed the reframe. Interface means a module public exported surface rather than the typescript interface keyword, so the tree runs from repository through inferred layers and modules to the exported surface and then to internals.

The internals level earns its place. Private top level symbols are sixty three percent of mermaid, seventy five percent of gstack, seventy percent of agent skills, and ninety one percent of herdr, so most code lives below the exported surface and a tree that stops at exports would hide the majority of it.

Symbol fan out inside a module is legible with a median of two to ten symbols and a ninetieth percentile of eleven to thirty one, though outliers reach eighty three to ninety seven. Mermaid has a median of two symbols across seven hundred sixty five modules, which suggests its module level is very fine grained and the inferred layer above it carries more of the meaning.
External packages are a toggleable view rather than always present nodes. The engineer can toggle them on and off or toggle into and out of them.

Topo performs no static analysis of its own. Parsing, import resolution, and symbol extraction are delegated to existing tools because operator confidence in getting that correct is low, and this session produced three independent scanner defects that support the caution.

Delegating all analysis conflicts with rendering an inferred logical view, because no existing tool produces inferred layers. Dependency cruiser yields modules and edges only, so a pure visual layer over another tool output would render the flat hairball the product exists to escape. The resolution is that static analysis is always delegated while graph transformation over the extracted graph is always ours, which restates the cycle six line that adapters lean into their sdk while the canonical

Spine edges remain undecided. The operator did not recognise the concept and it was explained as a graph property rather than static analysis, comparable to a critical path, computed from an already extracted graph at negligible cost. A decision is deferred.

Alignment offered and verified. The operator confirmed the exported surface reframe, chose a toggleable external packages view, ruled out performing static analysis in house, and selected a proof of concept as the next workflow.
Cycle eight handoff persisted and reread with all eight sections present. The tree shape is grounded end to end in measurement.
Frontier is needs proof of concept. Reading has exhausted what it can settle about the symbol level, and the exported surface and internal call graph can only be answered by exercising ts morph.
Prototype framed to test whether ts morph can extract a module exported surface and intra module call graph deterministically against a repository with no node modules installed.

Extraction succeeded on six hundred fifty one mermaid files in three seconds, producing five hundred sixty seven modules, three thousand one hundred eighty eight top level symbols, one thousand four hundred sixty one exported, and three thousand four hundred ninety four internal edges. Two consecutive runs produced byte identical output, so determinism holds at the symbol level.

The cycle eight export taxonomy was substantially wrong and ts morph corrected it. On an identical file set the two approaches agree exactly on interfaces at three hundred seventy three and types at one hundred thirty eight and differ by one on classes, but grep counted three hundred thirty three functions and five hundred seventy nine constants where ts morph finds six hundred thirty five functions and two hundred eighty values. Fifty two percent of what grep classified as a data constant is an

Symbol resolution works without node modules. Across ninety nine sampled modules there were zero unresolvable identifiers, because the binder resolves same file symbols even with resolution disabled. Naive name matching agrees with real resolution only ninety three point six percent of the time, so resolution rather than name matching should be used. Filtering property access names removed only zero point six percent of edges, so shadowing rather than property access is the dominant error source

The internals level is empty for forty one percent of mermaid modules, which have no internal edges at all. Internal edges per module have a median of one, a ninetieth percentile of seventeen, and a maximum of one hundred thirty one. This follows from the earlier observation that mermaid modules hold a median of two symbols.

The fail loudly on implausible zero guard was implemented and verified. Passing a bare directory rather than a glob reproduced the cycle five defect and the prototype exited with a non zero status rather than reporting success.
The forty seven megabyte prototype workspace was deleted, scripts and a sample extraction were preserved to the session workspace, and the mermaid checkout was verified to have no modified files.
The operator adopted ts morph for the symbol level. Recommendation adopt was accepted.

Two gaps remain between the current evidence and autonomous implementation. Layer inference has only ever run over rust crate manifests with sixty eight nodes and has never been run over a typescript module graph at the five hundred sixty seven module scale, where mermaid known cycle between diagrams and diagram api would condense. The interactive drill down and the external packages toggle have never been prototyped at all, since the earlier prototype rendered a static eight node diagram.

Dependency cruiser eighteen point two must be run with the repository root as the working directory. Run from elsewhere it emits unresolved relative specifiers as module nodes and still exits zero. It also rejects a reporter options json key that its own documentation implies. This is the fourth and fifth instance of a scanner appearing successful while returning wrong or partial results.

Dependency cruiser did not resolve typescript ecmascript module specifiers ending in js under any configuration tried, leaving only two hundred twenty eight of two thousand one hundred eight internal edges resolved. An adapter fixup that rewrites the extension and checks the file system recovered one thousand eight hundred eighty edges, so eighty nine percent of the module graph was missing from raw tool output.

Levelling at typescript module scale does not produce a legible logical view. Five hundred twenty nine modules and two thousand one hundred eight edges produced twenty five levels, with one level holding one hundred thirty three modules and many levels holding one or two. The result is strata rather than architecture.

The assumption that codebases are hierarchical is contradicted by the primary target. Mermaid holds one hundred sixty two of five hundred twenty nine modules inside six cycles, thirty one percent of the codebase, with a largest cycle of ninety three modules that contains no barrel files and is therefore genuine. Cyclic codebases cannot remain parked.

Spine edges are validated and are the strongest product finding of the session. Removing a single import from rendering util types to rendering util rendering elements shapes reduces modules held in cycles from one hundred sixty two to seventy seven and the largest cycle from ninety three to fifty four, freeing eighty five modules. A types module depending on an implementation module is an obvious architectural smell that no existing view would surface.
The prototype workspace was deleted, the adapter, leveller, and extracted graph were preserved to the session workspace, and the mermaid checkout was verified to have no modified files.

Collapsing each cycle into a single node improves individual levels but does not rescue levelling. The one hundred thirty three module level becomes forty one nodes, yet there are still twenty five levels and seven of them remain wider than fifteen nodes.

A dominator tree over the module graph is a far better navigation spine than levelling. Every module is reachable, the tree has one hundred thirty three internal nodes and three hundred ninety six leaves, median fan out is one, ninetieth percentile is five, and only three nodes exceed fifteen children. It is deterministic, inferred from code, and path free, which satisfies every constraint the operator set for the component browser.

The dominator tree recovers semantically real components. The shapes module exclusively owns eighty two modules and the diagram orchestration module exclusively owns sixty nine, which correspond to the shape library and the diagram type registry rather than arbitrary strata.

The root of the dominator tree has seventy five children, of which sixty one own nothing and fourteen own a subtree. Bucketing the sixty one shared leaves would leave a root view of roughly fifteen components.

The operator supplied an icepanel context diagram as a visual target. It shows a breadcrumb across three diagram levels, a version selector offering current plus one, external systems rendered as terminal nodes with vendor identity, semantically labelled edges, and a bottom bar of toggleable tag overlays for hostnames, region, accessibility, technology, status, and teams.

The icepanel target is a hand authored model rather than a derived one, so its cleanliness is the product of human curation. Topo derives everything from code and therefore cannot reproduce semantic edge labels such as pay with credit card, and can only approach that node density at coarse granularity.
Cycle ten handoff persisted and reread with all eight sections present. Dominance replaces levelling as the navigation spine.

All six requested behaviours work. Drilling from the repository into the shapes component moved from twenty eight children to eighty two, the breadcrumb returned to twenty eight, clicking an aggregated edge revealed three hundred twenty one underlying imports, the external toggle surfaced ten packages with usage counts led by d3 at seven modules, cycles render as dashed warning nodes, and spine edges render in red.

Spine edges were computed for all four significant tangles and three of the four are a low level module importing a high level one. A types module reaching into an implementation module frees eighty five modules, a rendering elements module importing the package entry point frees forty seven, and a diagram api types module frees five. This is a nameable architectural smell rather than an abstract graph property.

Both metaphors fail at the root view for the same reason, which is edge density rather than visual style. The box layout is four thousand ten pixels wide against a fifteen hundred pixel tall canvas and sprawls, while the hex map is compact at eight hundred thirteen by seven hundred sixty eight pixels but its regions are visually indistinct, its labels collide, and it draws no connections at all.

Aggregated edge weight is heavily skewed and filtering rescues the view. The root has one hundred twenty edges carrying one thousand three hundred sixty seven underlying imports with a median weight of one and a maximum of three hundred twenty one. Keeping only edges heavier than ten leaves fifteen edges, thirteen percent of the total, which still carry eighty three percent of all imports. A derived view can reach authored diagram density by thresholding rather than by curation.

Marking a node with the size of the tangle it belongs to is misleading. Nineteen of twenty eight root children carry a tangle badge because they are mutually entangled with each other, so the tangle exists between siblings rather than inside any one of them and should be drawn as a grouping rather than a per node badge.

A bounded research thread on aplas returned a cited report covering product shape, map model, navigation, ingestion, publishing, licensing, reusability, prior art, and stability. Several documentation pages were inaccessible and the terms of service are login gated, so licensing detail beyond published pricing is undetermined.

Aplas documentation claims that stability is what separates a map from a graph, stating that a graph relays itself out whenever data changes while a map keeps its coordinates so that what a viewer learned last month still holds. It names three maintenance modes and argues for stateful maintenance in which existing positions are loaded before the layout simulation runs.

That claim contradicts the earlier decision that saved layouts are not priority zero. Determinism was accepted as a substitute for stability, but cycle seven measured that determinism does not imply stability, so topo currently promises reproducibility rather than spatial memory. If the cited argument holds, a topo without persisted coordinates is a graph rather than a map.

Aplas regions are derived from grouping relations in the data rather than from geometry, integration channels collapse all connections between a pair into one bundled channel, and routing is constrained to the six hex directions in imitation of transit map cartography. A region buffer control sets the radius in hex cells drawn around each asset.

The prototype independently arrived at two of those mechanisms, since aggregated edges collapse all imports between a pair into one weighted edge and the dominator tree supplies the grouping relation that regions need. Six direction routing and the buffer radius were not implemented and are the missing pieces of the hex view.

Aplas is commercial software as a service with a free tier capped at fifty assets and paid tiers from one hundred ninety five dollars monthly. No open source component, self hosted option, or public patent or trademark notice was found. The report judges the hex grid, region derivation, bundled routing, layer based styling, multi scale zoom, and stability biased incremental layout to be general techniques, while naming the physics parameters, style schema, brand names, and specific routing algor

No solution to the retiling problem is documented by aplas. Automatic maps accept bounded drift through stability tuned physics and manual maps avoid the problem by requiring human placement, so the concern raised earlier about cartogram instability is unresolved even by the commercial reference product.

An optional artificial intelligence module may name components and layers, rank which views matter most, propose the initial grouping of modules, and propose initial spatial placement for a human to freeze. It adds logical wrappers around definitive code, for example sorting fifty five top level modules into a number of generic groups that it also determines. It must never lie about the architecture and it must always be clear where it is assisting.
